comment: Mutation targets: (target file, test command) pairs. 'before' runs only the module tests that existed before the tiered tests (their kernel/Makefile recipes, rebuilt by tests/harness/tiers.py); 'after' adds the tiered tests. Commands run from the repository root. 'lines' limits a large file to the part in scope; 'host' means the lines this host compiles (platform-only #if branches left out), recomputed on every run so the entry never needs editing when the file changes. 'ci' is the small fixed subset the CI job gates on; its baselines are the measured 'after' scores (tests/MUTATION_REPORT.md).

ci.baseline_note: measured 'after' scores on p10-integrate (tests/MUTATION_REPORT.md), rounded down to 4 places: rmag_core 86/90 (after the F-RMAG-OVF fix and its tests), fs_malloc 30/36, settle 175/197 (the 22 survivors are equivalent: array sizes, ties in the payer/payee pick, a loose loop bound, a dead NULL branch); zxv_engine 334/377 measured locally but 323/377 on the ubuntu-22.04 runner (twice, same count): the extra local kills are mutants that read uninitialized stack (a 31-byte seed copy, an out-of-range bucket index) or defensive re-checks of the abacus output, whose outcome depends on the machine, so the baseline is the runner's measurement; lpres_hex 184/211 (the 27 survivors are equivalent: array sizes, masks of already-masked values, ties between equal ranks, a hash buffer larger than needed, seq shifts that only differ past 127 records); mk_pay 119/130 (the 11 survivors are equivalent: array sizes, the static assert, seq bytes above 2^56, a loop bound reading a zeroed line, the always-zero escrow line of an invoice); vhub 281/296 (the 15 survivors are equivalent: array and buffer sizes, a tag copy whose extra byte is overwritten, a seed copy whose extra byte is overwritten by the tag, severity values that only set an order, running the default no-rule tag twice, an unreachable vbills == 0 and an unreachable zero quote step, the sign of a negative not-found index). Workers now get their own ZXV_TMP, so make-driven targets no longer race on /tmp paths; swarm_denom 468/473 (the 5 survivors are equivalent: a saturation check whose two branches return the same UINT64_MAX, the canonical-compare loop skipping tier 0 (two equal-value wallets cannot differ only there), the Fibonacci index search starting at 1 instead of 2, a pos > cap check already covered by the room check, and a loop start that only writes a bit the closing 1 then overwrites); zxvd_rpc 552/743 measured locally with the swarm earnings bridge (74.3%; was 492/677; gate 0.74; runs in .github/workflows/zxvd.yml, own_job, not in ci.yml's subset). Its 191 survivors are equivalent or need a fault the test cannot cause: buffer and array sizes, the private unit's minor units (only whole-unit amounts are posted), the earnings accounts failing to open (libzxv only refuses them for a disabled currency, which earn_open already rules out), -1 vs -2 error returns the callers only test against 0, descriptor checks that differ only at fd 0, stderr wording, allocation/socket/accept/mkdir failures, the libzxv version and context-creation failure paths, CR stripping (JSON already treats CR as whitespace), parameter readers returning true after the error is already recorded (the reply is the same error), cap/ctx destroy (a leak, not a behaviour), partial sends that need a client stalled past the 2 s send timeout, and the macOS-only peer check); merged with #69 and the aipi.* methods zxvd_rpc measures 1123+25/1520 (75.5%), gate kept at 0.74; with the method groups, feature switches and saved switches (zxvd_ext.h) it measures 1453+24/1940 (76.1%), gate kept at 0.74; with files.*, spaces.*, phone.*, play.* and the jurisdiction host merged (batch 2), 2028+24/2760 (74.4%, after the play.* unit test), gate kept at 0.74; zxvd_aipi 137/213 (64.3%; gate 0.62, own_job in zxvd.yml; a first run on a smaller mutant set scored 36/58). Its survivors are equivalent or need a fault the test cannot cause: buffer sizes (the reason text, the network buffer), defensive checks that cannot fire (a CID that fails to print, a route outside the table, a result that is not 8 bytes under the Z-Wasm call ABI, a publish that fails after the descriptor passed its check), values every path overwrites (job, in_len), the bounty/now/ttl of a call that never reaches the mesh, the cap version and the budget denominator of a 2^40 budget, /dev/urandom failing to open, and the NULL guards in close (destroy and free accept NULL) zxvd_cards 291/338 and zxvd_ident 191/238 (measured with the per-worker warm-up build in mutate.py, without which first builds hit the timeout and most mutants counted as compile errors); their survivors are buffer and array sizes, {0} initializers, the state-name table bounds, status counters, the ISO 8583 field loop bound, the +/-1 edges of the time range, return values after a failure is already recorded, ties in seq-based challenge eviction and an unreachable client-data-hash failure (the origin is validated first).; zxvd_econ 369/487 (75.8%; gate 0.75, own_job in zxvd.yml). Its 118 survivors are equivalent or need a fault the test cannot cause: buffer and array sizes (hash inputs, chip ids, the 8192-byte snapshot buffer, the kind buffer's spare byte), the stand-in signature and posting-id constants (the local sign is only checked against itself, and ids stay unique whichever bytes feed them, as does seq-- for seq++), the system accounts' and holders' opening flags and owners (no test-visible effect on an in-memory ledger), engine refusals the RPC layer rules out first (SVAULT_ERR_LEDGER, a switch the engine accepts), parameter readers returning true after the error is already recorded (the reply is the same error), loop bounds reading a zeroed holder or position slot, sizeof table counts, and ready() checks on methods whose fresh output is the same before and after setup (zenny.status, zenny.check, stats.status); zxvd_instruments 259/318 (81.4%; after clang-format of the changed lines 257/318, 80.8%, gate 0.80), zxvd_estate 505/651 (77.6%; gate 0.77) and zxvd_sandbox (the shared sandbox helpers) 100/138 (72.5%; gate 0.72), own_job in zxvd.yml. Their survivors are equivalent or need a fault the tests cannot cause: buffer and table sizes (kind, side and key buffers, the status-name tables and their unknown-status fallback, MAX_KEYS), the asset minor digits nothing prints, defensive returns after a reader already failed the call (the framework keeps the first error), engine and ledger failures that cannot happen on a fresh sandbox book (account and asset opens, a second refusal after the first), the sha256-derived idempotency and UETR bytes of a sandbox issue, and array-length checks the framework already enforces (MAX_TOK limits grants.distribute and estate heirs below the engine caps); zxvd_companion 44/51 (86.3%; gate 0.86, own_job in zxvd.yml). Its 7 survivors are equivalent: the snapshot's memset fill byte (the source overwrites the whole struct), snap returning true after the call already failed (the framework keeps the first error), the emoji buffer size and the METHODS[0] in the table count, and the UTF-8 lead byte's shift (18 vs 17 or 19: every palette code point is below U+40000, so the top bits are 0) and the first continuation byte's 0x80 vs 0x81 (cp >> 12 is 0x1F for the whole palette, bit 0 already set); zxvd_web4 333/373 (89.3%; gate 0.89, own_job in zxvd.yml; 44 compile errors not counted). Its 40 survivors are equivalent or need a fault the test cannot cause: buffer and array sizes (kind, tool, name, rnd and nonce buffers, the 4-byte magic compare), {0} initializers of values every path overwrites, the seed wipe after keygen (no visible effect), the +/-1 edges of the year-9999 'now' bound, the feed's eviction and lookup loop starts, a consent check that cannot fail on a token zxvd has just issued (only W4_ERR_SPACE is reachable: the 64-token log), the draw order of a denial, and the answer format's version byte offsets; zxvd_seats 515/627 (82.1%; gate 0.82, own_job in zxvd.yml; 101 compile errors not counted). Its 112 survivors are equivalent or need a fault the test cannot cause: buffer and array sizes (ids, names, passphrases, the temporary path, the file and line buffers), wipes of memory that is freed next (the Argon2id area, the roster, the undo copy, the read buffer), allocation failures (the roster, the Argon2id memory, the undo copy, the text), fdopen and fsync failures, the Windows-only helpers (not compiled on Linux), -1 vs -2 returns compared only with 0 or >= 0, initial values every path overwrites, the growth factor and first capacity of the roster, the first slot and tie order of session eviction (an unused slot has seq 0 either way), parameter readers returning true after the error is already recorded (the reply is the same error), the wait clamp at exactly the maximum, and a fails/t index swap the file test cannot tell apart once the back-off has started; zxvd_power 91/144 (63.2%; gate 0.63, own_job in zxvd.yml; 13 compile errors not counted). Its 53 survivors are equivalent or need a fault the test cannot cause: the Windows-only GetProcessTimes path (not compiled on Linux), the seconds term of the process CPU clock (the test process stays under one second of CPU), clock and host-reader failures (zph_open and zph_app only fail on NULL or a full 512-consumer ledger), the report buffer and table sizes, a tick or a note while closed (the ledger is not readable then), parameter readers returning true after the error is already recorded (the reply is the same error), consumer id 0 (always the system, never an agent or a found app) and want_uj 0 vs 1 against whole-microjoule budgets
